title: Federal Rule 13 — counterclaims and crossclaims
summary: A counterclaim is a claim against an opposing party. Rule 13 distinguishes compulsory claims arising from the relevant transaction or occurrence from permissive claims that may be asserted without that connection.

sections.Role in the course: A counterclaim is a claim against an opposing party. Rule 13 distinguishes compulsory claims arising from the relevant transaction or occurrence from permissive claims that may be asserted without that connection.
sections.What to examine: Identify the opposing party, the factual relationship, the time the claim existed, and any applicable exception. Then examine jurisdiction. Heyward-Robinson illustrates both the breadth and the disagreement surrounding a logical-relationship approach.
